summary: RFC 7865 and RFC 7866 disagree about how SIPREC recording metadata should be labeled, and neither registered the new media type. This RFC corrects that and registers the media type.

plainLanguage.summary: Two SIPREC specifications used different names for the same recording metadata. This RFC makes RFC 7866 use the name from RFC 7865 and registers that media type with IANA.

questions: which siprec media type is correct
subtitle: SIPREC metadata uses application/rs-metadata+xml, now registered with IANA.

tldr.problem: RFC 7865 and RFC 7866 gave different names for SIPREC recording metadata, and neither registered the media type.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9806 replaces each occurrence of application/rs-metadata in RFC 7866 with application/rs-metadata+xml and registers the media type.
tldr.outcome: The corrected name aligns RFC 7866 with RFC 7865 and resolves the reported inconsistency.

today: RFC 9806 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 7866. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Metadata Naming Conflict
sections.content:
The SIP-based Media Recording (SIPREC) protocol is defined by RFC 7865 and RFC 7866. RFC 7865 names the metadata type application/rs-metadata+xml, while RFC 7866 used application/rs-metadata.

RFC 7865 defines SIPREC metadata, and an erratum was filed against RFC 7866. Neither RFC had registered the media type with IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: The two SIPREC documents assigned different media type names to recording metadata. This RFC resolves the difference by aligning the protocol document with the metadata document.

sections.title: The Update to RFC 7866
sections.content:
Every instance of application/rs-metadata in RFC 7866 is replaced with application/rs-metadata+xml. This makes the label agree with RFC 7865.

The update clarifies the published documents and does not introduce security considerations beyond those listed in RFC 7866.
sections.plainLanguage: Use application/rs-metadata+xml wherever the older RFC 7866 name appeared. The update does not add new security considerations.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.content:
IANA registers type application and subtype rs-metadata+xml. The registration has no required or optional parameters, and its encoding considerations match application/xml as specified in RFC 7303.

Session Recording Clients and Session Recording Servers use the type. Its intended usage is COMMON, with no restrictions on where it can be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The official media type is application/rs-metadata+xml. The registration identifies the systems that use it and gives its XML encoding considerations.
